html:
Hawker centres are open-air food courts in Singapore where many small stalls sell cheap cooked food. In 2020 UNESCO listed Singapore's hawker culture as intangible heritage.

From the late 1960s the government moved street hawkers, who had sold food from carts and roadsides since the 19th century, into covered centres with water and drains. Most housing estates of the Housing and Development Board got one.

The stalls serve dishes such as chicken rice, laksa, char kway teow, satay and roti prata, blending the cooking of Chinese, Malay and Indian migrants; see Chinese migration. They are where Singaporeans of all classes eat, and are shared heritage with Malaysia.
sum: Hawker centres are open-air food courts in Singapore where many small stalls sell cheap cooked food. In 2020 UNESCO listed Singapore's hawker culture as intangible heritage.
